subject: Remove bundled PuTTYNG, auto-detect official PuTTY instead
body:
Remove bundled PuTTYNG, auto-detect official PuTTY instead

mRemoteNG previously shipped a bundled PuTTYNG.exe and defaulted to
launching it. A bundled, patched SSH client is a supply-chain
liability for an app that hands SSH credentials to remote hosts -
remove it and rely on the user's own official PuTTY install.

- New Tools/PuttyLocator: finds putty.exe via registry App Paths,
  Program Files\PuTTY, or PATH. GeneralAppInfo.PuttyPath is now a
  cached auto-detect result (empty string if none found) instead of
  a hardcoded "<install dir>\PuTTYNG.exe".
- Options > Advanced: "Browse" is now a folder picker that resolves
  putty.exe from the chosen directory (PuttyLocator.ResolveFromDirectory),
  and a "Download official PuTTY" link opens Simon Tatham's site.
- First run: if no PuTTY is detected and no custom path is set,
  frmMain opens Options > Advanced (PromptForPuttyIfMissing) so the
  user can point at their install or download one.
- PuttyBase: removed the VaultOpenbao SSH-OTP -auth-plugin injection
  path, which only worked by launching a PuTTYNG-specific helper
  plugin and is the only credential path that required PuTTYNG
  specifically. The credential-provider architecture (Secret Server,
  Passwordstate, 1Password, VaultOpenbao KV/LDAP) and the VaultOpenbao
  connector are unaffected - OTP secrets now flow through the normal
  -pwfile pipe like every other provider.
- Removed PuTTYNG.exe from the repo and from the build/installer
  (mRemoteNG.csproj, FilesFragment.wxs).

The dormant PuttyTypeDetector/_isPuttyNg embedding branches in
PuttyBase (for the case a user does point at a PuTTYNG build) are left
in place - they're inert without such a binary and removing them would
mean reworking the window-embedding code unnecessarily.

security_flags.reason: committed binary cannot be reviewed (OpenSSF Scorecard)
added code spawns a process or evaluates a string as code
a new or repointed package can pull arbitrary code at restore time
installer content ships signed to end users

triage.rationale: Removes bundled PuTTYNG; contrary to our design — we maintain robertpopa22/PuTTYNG and ship it intentionally. Also strips fork-specific Vault code.
